Life table from a vector of probabilities

Source: R/3_demographicFunctions.R
probs2lifetable.Rd

Create a lifetable object from a vector of one-year survival or death probabilities, starting at age 0. Useful for feeding mortality projections produced by other software (e.g. StMoMo) into lifecontingencies.

Usage

probs2lifetable(probs, radix = 10000, type = "px", name = "ungiven")

Arguments

probs

Numeric vector of one-year survival or death probabilities, starting at age 0. Its last element must be 0 when type is "px" (nobody survives beyond \(\omega\)) or 1 when type is "qx" (everyone alive at \(\omega\) dies within the last year); otherwise the function appends the missing terminal value and warns via cat().

radix

Initial cohort size \(l_0\). Default 10000.

type

Either "px" (survival) or "qx" (death) probabilities.

name

Character string stored in the @name slot of the returned object.

Value

A lifetable object.

Details

The limiting age \(\omega\) is the length of probs. The survival factor at age \(k\) is probs[k] (if type = "px") or 1 - probs[k] (if type = "qx"), and \(l_x\) is built as the cumulative product of these factors times radix.

References

Actuarial Mathematics (Second Edition), 1997, by Bowers, N.L., Gerber, H.U., Hickman, J.C., Jones, D.A. and Nesbitt, C.J.

See also

lifetable, actuarialtable

Author

Giorgio A. Spedicato

Examples

fakeSurvivalProbs <- seq(0.9, 0, by = -0.1)
newTable <- probs2lifetable(fakeSurvivalProbs, type = "px", name = "fake")
head(newTable)
#>   x    lx
#> 1 0 10000
#> 2 1  9000
#> 3 2  7200
#> 4 3  5040
#> 5 4  3024
#> 6 5  1512
tail(newTable)
#>    x        lx
#> 5  4 3024.0000
#> 6  5 1512.0000
#> 7  6  604.8000
#> 8  7  181.4400
#> 9  8   36.2880
#> 10 9    3.6288
